nodes.label: Patient has had difficulty breathing, cough, and expectoration for more than 30 days, accompanied by fever for more than 15 days
A 67-year-old male patient with past medical history of hyperuricemia for 5 years and allergies to tetracycline and oxytetracycline
Physical examination revealed breathing difficulties, cough, and multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and abdomen regions
Chest CT shows anterior mediastinal cavities and bilateral lower lung nodules
Lymph node biopsy reveals proliferative lymphoid tissue with large atypical cells, mitoses, and vascular/adipose infiltration
Laboratory tests show mildly elevated CA125 with normal AFP and CEA
Peripheral T-cell lymphoma / ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma
Other non-lymphoma malignancy (e.g., thymoma, carcinoma, sarcoma)
Pathologist interprets biopsy as consistent with aggressive B-cell lymphoma
Immunohistochemistry (CD20/Ki-67) is still pending for definitive subtyping
Pathologist states chronic infection and autoimmune disease are largely excluded by morphology
